brief_summary:
Background:

\- During puberty, children begin to develop into adults. Problems with the hormones released during puberty can affect the reproductive system. Some people have low hormone levels that severely delay or prevent puberty. Others start puberty abnormally early. Other people may have a normal puberty but develop reproductive disorders later in life. Researchers want to study people with reproductive disorders to learn more about how these disorders may be inherited.

Objectives:

\- To

eligibility_table.criterion: failure to go through a normal, age-appropriate, spontaneous puberty and low sex steroid levels in the setting of low/normal gonadotropins (due to substantial variability among patient presentations, this will be based on the clinical judgement of the Investigator)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not gone through normal puberty and has low testosterone levels with low GnRH, fitting the inclusion criterion.
The patient shows no signs of early puberty development, which is contrary to the criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: normal puberty with subsequent development of low gonadotropin levels
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has not experienced normal puberty, thus cannot meet this criterion.

eligibility_table.criterion: individuals with features indicating an increased risk of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's conditions and lab values indicate a high risk for hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

eligibility_table.criterion: Family members: both affected and unaffected family members are strongly encouraged to participate
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about family members, making it unclear if this criterion is met.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Have both affected and unaffected family members of the patient agreed to participate in the study?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients who have additional pituitary deficiencies, effectively ruling out isolated GnRH deficiency, whether these deficiencies are congenital or acquired (e.g. secondary to malignancy, infection, or irradiation)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient does not have additional pituitary deficiencies, indicating isolated GnRH deficiency.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patients who are taking medications known to affect GnRH secretion, such as corticosteroids or continuous opiate administration (or were taking them at the time of diagnosis)
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is not taking any medications that affect GnRH secretion.
